_comment: Developer tool storage on Windows, listed where it lives (AGENTS.md: patterns are data). The Windows twin of the Mac's developer-storage.json (Xcode and simulators): same format. action: trash = may be added to Cleanup (the Recycle Bin); guide = the tool's own command or settings, shown to copy, never run; never = nothing to do. perChild = one row per child folder; keepNewest = suggest keeping the highest version per folder. Paths take %LOCALAPPDATA%, %USERPROFILE%, %ProgramFiles%, %ProgramData% and ~; a trailing * in the last component matches by prefix. Sizes come from the scan, so a path outside the scanned folder is left out.

entries.title: WSL distributions
entries.why: Each Linux distribution lives in one virtual disk (ext4.vhdx) with every file inside it. Moving the folder to the Recycle Bin deletes the distro.
steps: Remove a distro you no longer need with wsl --unregister <name>. That deletes it and everything inside.
The disk doesn't shrink when you delete files inside it: run wsl --shutdown, then compact the .vhdx.

entries.title: Docker Desktop disk
entries.why: Every image, container, volume and build cache Docker Desktop keeps, inside one virtual disk. Moving it to the Recycle Bin wipes Docker's data.
steps: Run the command to remove stopped containers, unused networks, dangling images and build cache, or use Docker Desktop's Troubleshoot › Clean / Purge data.

entries.title: Android emulators
entries.why: Every emulator with its apps and data. Moving one to the Recycle Bin by hand leaves Android Studio with a broken device.
steps: Delete emulators you no longer use in Android Studio › Device Manager.

entries.title: Android system images
entries.why: Whole Android versions for the emulator, one per API level. An emulator built on one stops working without it.
steps: Remove the ones no emulator uses in Android Studio › SDK Manager. The newest is marked KEEP.

entries.title: .NET SDKs
entries.why: .NET SDKs installed side by side. Each update adds one; the older ones stay until you remove them.
steps: Uninstall older SDKs in Settings › Apps › Installed apps. The newest is marked KEEP.

entries.title: NuGet HTTP cache
entries.why: Package downloads NuGet keeps to make restores faster. It downloads them again when a restore needs them.
steps: Safe to add to Cleanup. It goes to the Recycle Bin first.
